correctness.rationale: The resolvent is a positive exponential mixture. The identity T=(R(theta h)-(1-theta)I)/theta reduces entrywise sign to strictly decreasing diagonal resolvents. Strong Markov regeneration gives R_ii(s)=[1+q_i s(1-E exp(-H_i/s))]^-1, strictly decreasing from 1 to pi_i, with strict positivity at the critical theta equality. Finite-state return moments establish R_ii(s)=pi_i+c_i/s+O(s^-2), and the crossing equation yields theta_c(theta_c-theta)h_c->min_{pi_i=pi_min}c_i. All boundaries and theta=0 are proved. Exact finite checker reproduced 63 generators and 2205 cases of each substantive class, not substituting for proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal guarantee h<=1/((1-theta)max_i q_i) is sufficient but is not a global exact threshold for a fixed Q; in fact h may be arbitrary when theta>=1-min pi. Classical monotonicity barriers concern all generators under a shared rate bound and therefore do not imply the present fixed-Q result. Explicit earlier directed-cycle and birth-death instances are proper subclasses, not stronger coverage. The previously established Crank–Nicolson Cayley-reduction covers the theta=1/2 diagonal criterion without needing regeneration; it is not claimed new and does not itself imply nonreversible strict diagonal-resolvent monotonicity for the whole theta family or the critical second-moment asymptotics.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither uniform SSP positivity constraints nor symmetric Dirichlet positivity imply the present finite irreducible Markov generator theorem. The new result has a weaker assumption on geometry (arbitrary directed nonreversible Q), sharp equality cases, strict finite cutoff, and return-time second-moment asymptotic. Its proof supplies all missing Markov-specific implications, and it does not claim that individual regenerative identities are new. The all-irreducible nonreversible theorem goes beyond the earlier Cayley identity and reversible spectral calculus because eigenvalue expansions with nonnegative coefficients are not generally available for nonreversible Q; regeneration supplies the missing strict monotonicity and its return-moment constant.

originality.rationale: Comparison with the detailed original Runge–Kutta positivity theory (Horváth 1998 and 2005) separates uniform method-class absolute-monotonicity radii from sharp fixed-generator Markov positivity. A relevant full-text sharp Crank–Nicolson heat problem has nonconservative Dirichlet boundaries; neither it nor class-uniform SSP theory implies the arbitrary row-conservative irreducible Q stationary-mass classification, unique finite threshold and return-time second-moment divergence. Previously established direct Cayley-resolvent criteria for Crank–Nicolson on arbitrary finite generators, reversible-chain spectral cutoffs, and the directed-cycle and birth–death subclass results are acknowledged as prior; only the all-parameter and nonreversible general crossing/moment law is assessed as an addition. Residual risk of a less discoverable equivalent specialized result remains.
residual_risks: Earlier fixed-generator theta-method results or a renewal-resolvent theorem in hard-to-search Markov process/numerical-analysis literature may imply this statement without matching terminology.

value.rationale: For every finite irreducible directed CTMC, all-positive-step probability preservation of the theta family is decided by min stationary mass alone; below it, one monotone scalar resolvent equation gives the exact crossing, while the return-time second moment controls its critical divergence. The theorem distinguishes universal geometric thresholds from network-dependent finite cutoffs and has real applications to stochastic integrators; it is a natural all-generator classification, not a small example or arbitrary invariant.
